title: GMAT Focus Data Insights Practice Test 5
instructions: Original exam-style practice test with answers and explanations.

questions.prompt: A graph showing loan approval rates in the banking sector presents the following data: Personal: 64%, Mortgage: 71%, Business: 48%, Auto: 79%, Student: 85%. According to the graph, which segment/period shows the highest value?
options: A. Cannot be determined from the data
E. The value closest to the overall average
questions.explanation: This graphics_interpretation question tests ability to interpret banking data on loan approval rates.

questions.prompt: Based on the chart of campaign conversion rates data (Email: 3.2%, Social: 1.8%, Search: 4.7%, Display: 0.9%, Referral: 6.1%), which TWO values would combine to equal approximately the average?
questions.explanation: This graphics_interpretation question tests ability to interpret marketing data on campaign conversion rates.

questions.prompt: A scatter plot comparing subscriber churn rates across telecommunications categories shows: Postpaid: 2.1%, Prepaid: 8.4%, Broadband: 1.7%, Enterprise: 0.8%. If the trend continued, which projection is most consistent?
options: B. The value closest to the overall average
C. Cannot be determined from the data
questions.explanation: This graphics_interpretation question tests ability to interpret telecommunications data on subscriber churn rates.

questions.prompt: A graph showing student assessment pass rates in the education sector presents the following data: Mathematics: 73%, Science: 68%, English: 81%, History: 77%, Languages: 62%. According to the graph, which segment/period shows the highest value?
questions.explanation: This graphics_interpretation question tests ability to interpret education data on student assessment pass rates.

questions.prompt: Analysis of claims processing times in insurance: Auto: 8.2 days, Home: 14.5 days, Health: 6.1 days, Life: 21.3 days. Select the value closest to the median AND the value that represents the greatest deviation from the mean.
questions.explanation: This two_part_analysis question tests ability to interpret insurance data on claims processing times.

dataContext.data: Auto: 8.2 days, Home: 14.5 days, Health: 6.1 days, Life: 21.3 days

questions.prompt: Given construction project completion on schedule data: Residential: 58%, Commercial: 44%, Infrastructure: 37%, Industrial: 51%. In the left column select the highest-performing category; in the right column select the category that improved most year-over-year.
questions.explanation: This two_part_analysis question tests ability to interpret construction data on project completion on schedule.

questions.prompt: A agriculture manager reviews crop yield indices: Wheat: 108, Corn: 95, Rice: 112, Soybeans: 103, Cotton: 89. Select: (1) the category requiring immediate attention and (2) the category that exceeds the target of the average by the greatest margin.
questions.explanation: This two_part_analysis question tests ability to interpret agriculture data on crop yield indices.

questions.prompt: Analysis of return rates by product category in e-commerce: Electronics: 12%, Clothing: 28%, Home goods: 8%, Books: 3%, Sports: 15%. Select the value closest to the median AND the value that represents the greatest deviation from the mean.
questions.explanation: This two_part_analysis question tests ability to interpret e-commerce data on return rates by product category.

dataContext.data: Electronics: 12%, Clothing: 28%, Home goods: 8%, Books: 3%, Sports: 15%

questions.prompt: Three data sources on consulting project profitability by industry are provided: (Memo) Overall performance improved this quarter. (Table) Technology: 24%, Finance: 31%, Healthcare: 18%, Government: 9%, Retail: 14%. (Email) Stakeholders express concern about outliers. Which source most directly supports the memo's claim?
options: D. All three sources are equally relevant
questions.explanation: This multi_source_reasoning question tests ability to interpret consulting data on project profitability by industry.

questions.prompt: Source 1 (Report): tourism visitor spending by activity shows: Accommodation: 38%, Food: 24%, Transport: 18%, Entertainment: 12%, Shopping: 8%. Source 2 (Email): The weakest performer needs a 20% improvement to meet targets. Source 3 (Table): Targets are set at the top-quartile value. Which category needs improvement?
options: E. All three sources are equally relevant
questions.explanation: This multi_source_reasoning question tests ability to interpret tourism data on visitor spending by activity.

questions.prompt: Reviewing recruitment records: Source A shows time-to-hire by department: Engineering: 47 days, Marketing: 31 days, Finance: 28 days, Sales: 22 days, HR: 19 days. Source B notes the average. Source C flags values more than 25% above or below average. Which values would Source C flag?
options: A. All three sources are equally relevant
questions.explanation: This multi_source_reasoning question tests ability to interpret recruitment data on time-to-hire by department.

dataContext.data: Engineering: 47 days, Marketing: 31 days, Finance: 28 days, Sales: 22 days, HR: 19 days

questions.prompt: Three data sources on environmental emissions reduction by sector are provided: (Memo) Overall performance improved this quarter. (Table) Energy: -14%, Transport: -8%, Industry: -6%, Agriculture: -3%, Buildings: -11%. (Email) Stakeholders express concern about outliers. Which source most directly supports the memo's claim?
options: B. All three sources are equally relevant
questions.explanation: This multi_source_reasoning question tests ability to interpret environmental data on emissions reduction by sector.

questions.prompt: What is the relative ranking of categories in retail banking product penetration rates? (1) Current accounts: 100%. (2) The remaining values follow a consistent trend.
options: A. Both statements together are sufficient, but neither alone is sufficient
B. Each statement alone is sufficient
C. Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
D. Statement (1) alone is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
E. Statement (2) alone is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
questions.explanation: This data_sufficiency question tests ability to interpret retail banking data on product penetration rates.

dataContext.data: Current accounts: 100%, Savings: 74%, Credit cards: 52%, Investments: 31%, Mortgages: 28%

questions.prompt: Is the streaming media content viewing patterns above the industry benchmark of the median? (1) Drama: 35%. (2) The range of all values is 10%.
options: A. Statement (2) alone is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
B. Both statements together are sufficient, but neither alone is sufficient
C. Each statement alone is sufficient
D. Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
E. Statement (1) alone is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
questions.explanation: This data_sufficiency question tests ability to interpret streaming media data on content viewing patterns.

questions.prompt: Can the average supply chain supplier performance scores be calculated precisely? (1) Quality: 87/100, Delivery: 79/100, Price: 83/100, Responsiveness: 91/100, Sustainability: 74/100. (2) All categories are measured using the same methodology.
options: A. Statement (1) alone is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
B. Statement (2) alone is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
C. Both statements together are sufficient, but neither alone is sufficient
D. Each statement alone is sufficient
E. Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
questions.explanation: This data_sufficiency question tests ability to interpret supply chain data on supplier performance scores.

questions.prompt: What is the relative ranking of categories in fitness gym membership usage? (1) Peak hours 6-8am: 42%. (2) The remaining values follow a consistent trend.
options: A. Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
B. Statement (1) alone is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
C. Statement (2) alone is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
D. Both statements together are sufficient, but neither alone is sufficient
E. Each statement alone is sufficient
questions.explanation: This data_sufficiency question tests ability to interpret fitness data on gym membership usage.

questions.prompt: Sort the cybersecurity incident response times table: Detection: 4.2h, Containment: 2.8h, Eradication: 6.1h, Recovery: 12.4h, Documentation: 3.9h. Which statement is accurate?
options: A. The ranking depends on the sort criterion
B. Insufficient data to determine rank
C. The first row ranks highest
D. The second row ranks highest
E. The third row ranks highest
questions.explanation: This table_analysis question tests ability to interpret cybersecurity data on incident response times.

questions.prompt: A table comparing property management occupancy rates by building type shows: Office A-grade: 94%, Office B-grade: 78%, Retail flagship: 97%, Retail secondary: 81%, Industrial: 89%. Indicate whether each statement is true, false, or cannot be determined.
options: A. The third row ranks highest
B. The ranking depends on the sort criterion
C. Insufficient data to determine rank
D. The first row ranks highest
E. The second row ranks highest
questions.explanation: This table_analysis question tests ability to interpret property management data on occupancy rates by building type.

dataContext.data: Office A-grade: 94%, Office B-grade: 78%, Retail flagship: 97%, Retail secondary: 81%, Industrial: 89%

options: A. The second row ranks highest
B. The third row ranks highest
